doc.title: Al Gafa interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, May 2, 2023

title: First recording sessions via Doc Pomus and Morty Shuman audition
summary: He got into session work after a doo-wop audition with Pomus and Shuman, was interrupted by Navy service, then resumed.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Session players on the hits: "I played on that record"

blocks.x: I love that. “We can’t start the session yet, Al’s on his way from high school.” You know this was on my list of topics because I’m fascinated by those recording sessions at the time. You had stated that in the early 60s money was being thrown around in the music business. Can you extrapolate on that a little bit?

Okay yeah. First of all my recording work started — I auditioned with a, it was a doo- wop group. They had an audition with two really well known artists, Doc Pomus and Morty Shuman. They wrote many Ray Charles hits and Andy Williams. They went to play an audition and they asked me to play the audition with them. And at the audition Morty Shuman, he was the keyboard player, he asked me if I would like to do recording sessions. So I’m just — it was a hobby of mine, yeah sure, okay, what’s a recording session? Let’s find out what it is. So I got started in the business like that. And when I graduated high school I went into the Navy and so I actually cut that recording session thing short because I went in the service. When I got out of the service I looked them up again and they threw me right back in and that’s how it started. Okay. Now I forgot the other part of your question.
